prompt:
Paint ONE place into this tile of a painted grand-strategy map. The input is the finished map around the place, seen straight down; the place stands at the exact CENTRE of the image.

The place: Thu Trì Thành, city. Paint it as a walled city: a rectangular wall with gate towers, dense grey-tile roofs inside, a central tower or palace, a market square, suburbs along the roads outside the walls.
How it looks: A walled port city where a river meets the sea below wooded hills, built in steps so that tiers of square stone pools descend through its streets from the upper town to the harbour. After night rain on the hills every pool brims and spills into the next, and the whole city murmurs. Over the lower terraces hang the dark oiled-paper awnings of the Night Rain Market, and a guardian array (hộ thành trận) shimmers faintly on the walls.
Art brief: A walled port city miniature on a gentle slope between wooded hills and the sea at a river mouth: grey-tile roofs in stepped rows, and the signature, a descending stair of square stone pools brimming with water between the streets, spilling from tier to tier down to the harbour. Dark oiled-paper awnings over the lowest terraces; a faint shimmer of array light along the walls; a few boats at the quay. Wet surfaces after rain, warm golden-hour light from the top left breaking through. No text, no figures larger than specks, nothing outside the footprint.

Rules:
- Paint the place as a small, finely detailed miniature, as if a model-maker had built it into this painted relief: seen from above at a gentle angle so roofs, walls and towers read clearly, its base sitting naturally on the terrain that is there (follow the slopes, the shore, the river).
- Keep it centred and compact: the whole place fits inside a circle about 22 % of the image width across the centre. Short roads or paths may lead out of it.
- Match the map exactly: the same golden-hour light from the TOP LEFT with soft shadows to the bottom right, the same painterly style, colours and level of detail as the surrounding terrain; the building scale fits the trees and hills around it.
- Leave everything outside that central circle exactly as it is in the input.
- Never: text, labels, banners with writing, flags with symbols, people larger than specks, a frame, a vignette, clouds over the place.
